full_text_en:
Chongqing Yubei District People's Procuratorate v. Hu Renguo

— illegal logging of state key protected plants

Case Summary

The act of illegally transplanting state key protected plants without obtaining a forest tree logging permit constitutes "illegal logging of state key protected plants" as provided for in Article 344 of the Criminal Law. Whether the defendant had subjective intent to illegally log state key protected plants may be determined by considering factors such as whether the wild plants have generally recognizable external features, whether the defendant has work experience in the forestry industry, and whether the nature reserve has installed special plant protection facilities.

Procuratorial Authority : Chongqing Yubei District People's Procuratorate.

Defendant : Hu Renguo, male, born December 30, 1953, of Han nationality, residing in Tuchang Town, Hechuan District, Chongqing. In this case, he was criminally detained on September 6, 2017, by the Beibei District Branch of Chongqing Public Security Bureau, released on bail pending trial on September 12, 2017, and arrested on March 16, 2018.

The Chongqing Yubei District People's Procuratorate charged the defendant Hu Renguo with the crime of illegal logging of state key protected plants and instituted a public prosecution with the Chongqing Yubei District People's Court.

The prosecutorial authority alleged that the defendant Hu Renguo's conduct constituted the crime of illegal logging of state key protected plants, and that he had the sentencing circumstances of voluntary surrender and attempted crime, recommending a fixed-term imprisonment of two to two years and six months, and a fine.

The defendant Hu Renguo had no objection to the alleged facts, the charge, and the sentencing recommendation, and signed the plea agreement. He also had no objection during the first-instance trial.

The Chongqing Yubei District People's Court found the following facts at first instance:

In March 2016, the defendant Hu Renguo contacted Guo (separately prosecuted) intending to purchase wild camphor trees. Guo then contacted Tan (separately prosecuted) to find tree sources. On May 18 of that year, without obtaining permission from the competent forestry authority, Hu Renguo, through Tan, reached a purchase and sale agreement with the Horticulture Branch of Chongqing Jinyunshan Horticulture Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jinyun Horticulture Company, also known as Jinguoyuan), and paid a deposit to the company. Subsequently, with the assistance of Guo and Tan, Hu Renguo organized workers to log 21 wild camphor trees within Jinguoyuan operated by the company, 29 wild camphor trees in the state-owned forest of Team No. 5 of the Daihu Protection Station of Chongqing Jinyunshan National Nature Reserve, and 72 wild camphor trees in the state-owned forest of Team No. 4 of the Chengjiang Protection Station of Chongqing Jinyunshan National Nature Reserve. According to appraisal, the 122 wild camphor trees were Class II state-protected wild plants, with a total volume of standing timber of 14.994 cubic meters.

It was further found that the defendant Hu Renguo logged the above wild camphor trees for the purpose of transplanting. At the time of the incident, only crown reduction and root treatment had been performed on the 122 camphor trees, and the transplanting had not yet been completed. No death of the camphor trees was found.

The Chongqing Yubei District People's Court held at first instance:

The prosecutorial authority's charge that the defendant Hu Renguo committed the crime of illegal logging of state key protected plants, which is a serious circumstance, was supported by clear facts and credible, sufficient evidence; the charge was established; the sentencing recommendation was appropriate and should be adopted. The defense counsel's opinions that Hu Renguo was a first-time offender, had the circumstance of voluntary surrender, was an attempted crime, and had a good attitude of admitting guilt, and that he should be given a lenient, lighter, or mitigated punishment, were adopted.

Accordingly, the Chongqing Yubei District People's Court, in accordance with Article 344, Article 23, Article 67(1), Article 52, and Article 53 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 1 and Article 2(1) of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Trial of Criminal Cases on Destroying Forest Resources, rendered the judgment on March 28, 2018:

Defendant Hu Renguo was found guilty of illegal logging of state key protected plants and sentenced to two years' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 30,000.

Hu Renguo, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Chongqing First Intermediate People's Court, contending: Hu Renguo was innocent; if guilty, a suspended sentence should be applied. Regarding the reasons for innocence: First, the appellant Hu Renguo was not the actor; his actions were on behalf of Chongqing Linya Horticultural Landscape Engineering Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Linya Company), and he lacked the objective elements of the crime. Second, Hu Renguo was deceived and used by Guo and Tan; he had no criminal intent himself, and there was no common intent with Guo and Tan; thus he lacked the subjective elements of the crime. Third, during the stage of review and prosecution, without any supplemental investigation evidence, Hu Renguo received the appraisal opinion served by the public security organ; he applied for a re-appraisal within the statutory period but received no response; the appraisal procedure was illegal, and the appraisal opinion contained content inconsistent with objective facts, so it should not be admitted. Fourth, Hu Renguo's conduct was not "logging" but "transplanting"; transplanting does not require administrative approval and did not cause adverse consequences to the subject matter; instead, it made the trees grow more luxuriant. In summary, Hu Renguo's conduct did not constitute a crime. Regarding the reasons for applying a suspended sentence: First, units and individuals with more serious conduct than Hu Renguo were not prosecuted; compared with Guo and Tan, who had already received criminal punishment, Hu Renguo's role and status were lesser. Second, he had statutory or discretionary circumstances such as voluntary surrender, attempted crime, first-time offender, and good attitude of admitting guilt, which were undisputed by both sides and recognized at first instance. Third, Hu Renguo was old and sick; as a grassroots cadre, he had a consistent good record and contributed to local economic and social development; his involvement in this case was due to deception, and he had no subjective malice. Fourth, the appraisal opinion erred in finding that the 21 camphor trees logged within Jinyuan Horticulture Company were also wild camphor trees; Jinyuan Horticulture Company is an enterprise engaged in nursery planting and management, so the trees within its area could not be wild. Fifth, Hu Renguo was willing to provide economic compensation to make amends. Moreover, there were procedural violations in this case: the plea agreement during the review and prosecution stage was signed by infringing on the suspect's and defense counsel's rights and through deception; at trial, the first-instance court did not organize cross-examination, delivered the judgment immediately after pronouncement, and collected a fine of RMB 30,000 from Hu Renguo's relatives before trial, which constituted prejudgment.

The procurator performing duties at the second instance opined that the first-instance judgment had clear facts, credible and sufficient evidence, legal procedures, correct conviction, and appropriate sentencing, and should be affirmed.

At the second-instance trial, the defense counsel of appellant Hu Renguo presented the following new evidence: (1) an EMS receipt, to prove that Hu Renguo applied for a re-appraisal within the statutory period; (2) photos and videos of the logging site, to prove that the felled trees did not die and were not "logged"; (3) a bank transfer slip, to prove that Hu Renguo was not the transaction subject; (4) a disability certificate (Grade IV physical disability) and a certificate of village committee director, to prove Hu Renguo's physical condition and character. The procurator submitted that some of the above evidence was submitted in court, violating relevant legal provisions, and its authenticity could not be verified; it was also irrelevant and could not achieve the proof purpose; the procurator did not recognize any of the defense counsel's submitted evidence. The court held that: as to evidence (1), because it could not prove its relevance to the case and could not achieve the proof purpose, it was not admitted; as to evidence (2), because the involved wild camphor trees numbered 122, the photos and videos of felled trees provided by the defense counsel were only a part and lacked corresponding probative force; moreover, whether the felled trees were completely transplanted or died did not affect the conviction in this case; the first-instance judgment had already considered this factor in finding Hu Renguo's conduct as an attempted crime, so this evidence could not be admitted as new evidence; as to evidence (3), whether Hu Renguo was the subject of the contract or the subject of the transfer only related to the mode of conduct of the timber transaction and did not affect the determination of the criminal facts in this case; this evidence could not achieve the proof purpose; as to evidence (4), it also could not achieve the proof purpose. Therefore, none of the above evidence was admitted.

Upon second instance, the Chongqing First Intermediate People's Court confirmed the facts found at first instance.

The Chongqing First Intermediate People's Court held at second instance:

The appeal opinions and reasons raised by the appellant Hu Renguo and his defense counsel were unfounded, as commented below:

I. Whether "transplanting" constitutes "logging"

The Criminal Law provision for the crime of illegal logging of state key protected plants does not explicitly define "logging." However, considering the legislative purpose of this crime and relevant national regulations, it can be deduced that illegal logging includes illegal transplanting. From the legislative purpose of the crime of illegal logging of state key protected plants, the object of this crime is the national forestry protection management system. Illegal transplanting of state key protected plants does not aim to destroy the plant's life for profit, but it destroys the original living environment of the plant and infringes upon national forest resources and ecological environment. Punishing such conduct is consistent with the legislative purpose of Article 344 of the Criminal Law. Moreover, in the case of unlicensed transplanting, although the transplanting subject subjectively hopes the transplanted plant will survive, because it is removed from state supervision, whether the transplanting subject has the necessary technical conditions and whether the operational methods are standardized cannot be guaranteed, and such conduct may increase the probability of plant death. Therefore, illegal transplanting should be brought within the regulatory scope of the crime of illegal logging of state key protected plants. From the perspective of relevant national regulations, Part 3(2) of the *Notice of the State Forestry Administration on Effectively Strengthening and Strictly Regulating the Management of Tree Digging and Transplanting* stipulates: "The management of digging trees and the transportation and management of dug trees shall apply the provisions of the *Forest Law* and the *Regulations on the Implementation of the Forest Law* concerning forest logging, timber transportation, and management (processing). Digging trees must obtain a forest tree logging permit." Moreover, the notice stated at the outset that it was formulated to protect forest resources and natural ecological environment in accordance with the law, and to effectively strengthen and strictly regulate the management of tree digging and transplanting. This shows that the competent administrative department considers logging to include digging and transplanting, and digging and transplanting also require a logging permit. Since the administrative department's definition of logging is professional and scientific, it should be referenced.

II. Whether the appraisal opinion and the first-instance procedure were lawful

First, as to whether the appraisal opinion was lawful. During the review and prosecution stage, a re-appraisal is not necessarily initiated upon the suspect's application. The prosecutorial authority, upon review, found that the reasons for re-appraisal were insufficient and decided not to conduct a re-appraisal; this act was not improper. The appraisal institution that issued the appraisal opinion in this case was the Chongqing Forestry Judicial Appraisal Center, and the conclusion was that the 122 involved camphor trees were wild camphor trees. The court found no illegality in the appraisal institution's qualification or the appraisal conclusion, and therefore admitted it. As to the 21 felled wild camphor trees within Jinguoyuan, their wild camphor tree nature cannot be denied simply because they grew within Jinguoyuan; there are no reasonable and sufficient reasons to question or overturn the appraisal opinion of a professional appraisal institution.

Second, as to whether the first-instance procedure was lawful. The appellant Hu Renguo and his defense counsel signed and fingerprinted the plea agreement; the prosecutorial authority clearly proposed a sentencing recommendation of two to two years and six months' imprisonment and a fine in the plea agreement. During the first-instance trial, the judge asked Hu Renguo whether the plea agreement reflected his true intention, and he confirmed it, which was sufficient to believe that the application of the lenient procedure based on admission of guilt and acceptance of punishment was in line with his true intention. In such circumstances, the first-instance court applied the expedited procedure to try the case and appropriately reflected the characteristics of the expedited procedure in the trial procedure; there was no procedural illegality.

III. Whether the appellant Hu Renguo's conduct satisfied the subjective and objective elements of the crime

The appellant Hu Renguo, as one of the actual partners, signed a seedling purchase and sale agreement with Linya Company in the name of Chongqing Baoguang Horticulture Farm. Hu Renguo's side was not only the supplier of trees but also responsible for providing labor for digging and transplanting for Linya Company. In the transaction, Hu Renguo specifically organized the supply of trees and organized workers to dig and transplant trees. For this purpose, Hu Renguo, through Guo and then through Tan, contacted the seller Jinyuan Horticulture Company and, based on the logging scope indicated by Tan et al., illegally logged 122 wild camphor trees. The above facts were proved by evidence including Hu Renguo's confession, the confessions of Guo and Tan, the testimony of Hu, Zhou, Xiang, et al., and contracts.

Regarding the appellant Hu Renguo's subjective intent to illegally log, the following is commented: There is an obvious difference in appearance between wild camphor trees and artificially planted camphor trees. Hu Renguo had work experience in the landscaping industry and should have been able to determine whether the logged objects were wild camphor trees. In addition, wild trees in the Jinyun Mountain Nature Reserve have biological control lamps, and a boundary marker stands between Jinguoyuan and the Jinyun Mountain National Nature Reserve. When Hu Renguo went to the site to inspect the camphor trees, Guo and others had informed him of these circumstances. Hu Renguo also confessed in the interrogation records that he knew the trees were wild camphor trees and knew that wild camphor trees were protected by the state, and he was also aware that his logging conduct was carried out without obtaining a logging permit.

The appellant Hu Renguo, knowing that neither he nor any party in the transaction had a forest tree logging permit, nevertheless organized workers to log wild camphor trees with the assistance of others. He had both subjective intent and objective conduct of illegally logging state key protected plants. He illegally logged 122 wild camphor trees, with a total volume of standing timber of 14.994 cubic meters, constituting the crime of illegal logging of state key protected plants.

IV. Whether a suspended sentence should be applied to the appellant Hu Renguo

The second-instance court held that a suspended sentence should not be applied to the appellant Hu Renguo. The reasons are as follows: First, the first-instance sentence already reflected a lighter or mitigated punishment. Article 2 of the *Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Trial of Criminal Cases on Destroying Forest Resources* provides that "illegally logging two or more precious trees or destroying precious trees causing the death of three or more precious trees" constitutes "serious circumstances." According to Article 344 of the Criminal Law, for "serious circumstances," a fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than seven years shall be imposed. In other words, illegally logging two or more precious trees should result in a fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years. In this case, the illegal logging of 122 wild camphor trees, which are Class II state-protected wild plants, far exceeds the baseline for "serious circumstances" and would ordinarily warrant a sentence of more than three years. However, considering the following factors: (a) compared with logging for timber, transplanting causes less damage to forest resources and may warrant a lighter punishment; (b) Hu Renguo is a first-time offender, has the circumstance of voluntary surrender, did not cause widespread death of the felled plants, and did not complete the entire transplanting, making his conduct an attempted crime; (c) at first instance, the lenient procedure based on admission of guilt and acceptance of punishment was applied; on the basis of Hu Renguo's admission of guilt and acceptance of punishment, the procuratorate's sentencing recommendation and the first-instance sentence both reflected the spirit of leniency, and Hu Renguo proactively paid the fine in advance; taking into account his status and role in the joint crime, the first-instance sentence of two years' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 30,000 was not improper. Second, during the second instance, Hu Renguo claimed that the first-instance procedure was illegal and that his admission of guilt and acceptance of punishment were obtained by the prosecutorial authority through deception, but he did not present any evidence to prove the procedural illegality; Hu Renguo also denied some basic criminal facts that he had previously confessed and that were confirmed by the first-instance court, but he did not provide a reasonable explanation or present corresponding evidence. Therefore, the court confirmed the facts found at first instance. Third, the grounds of appeal raised by Hu Renguo and his defense counsel concerning Hu Renguo's physical condition and good character are not statutory grounds for applying a suspended sentence. In summary, this case does not meet the conditions for applying a suspended sentence, and a suspended sentence should not be applied.

In conclusion, the original judgment had clear facts, credible and sufficient evidence, correct application of law, appropriate sentencing, and lawful trial procedures. The Chongqing First Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with Article 225(1)(1) of the *Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China*, rendered the ruling on July 24, 2018:

Appeal dismissed; original judgment affirmed.
